correctness.rationale: For an abelian p-group with conjugate partition r_j, exactly p^s_j-p^s_(j-1) elements have order p^j, each cyclic subgroup has p^j-p^(j-1) generators and p^(2j)-p^(2j-2) ordered generating pairs. Summing produces N=1+(p+1)Σ p^(j-1+s_(j-1))(p^r_j-1). The supports of the base-p digit blocks occupy precisely r_j positions and have one zero gap, yielding iff recognition. For rank at least two, N≡-p mod p², giving denominator p^(2n-1) exactly and recovering the previously unknown p and n. The inverse constructs a partition, and a second application of the exact count confirms the desired probability. Both cyclic boundary and nonabelian scope restrictions are explicit. Exact checker tested 3445 partitions plus direct group-element pairs in 40 small groups; the proof does not rely on finite tests.

evidence: For any p-group, Dedekind psi of a nonidentity p-power order is (p+1)/p times that element order. Therefore the cyclic-pair statistic is affinely related to the element-order sum.
Amiri (2026), Corollary 3.2, and earlier Tărnăuceanu: for abelian p-groups of a prescribed same order, the element-order sum determines isomorphism type.

The new iff condition recognizes which rationals arise without pre-supplying the prime, group order, or invariant partition, using a precise digit language. The existing rigidity statements do not provide or logically directly state this image-membership test; it requires the explicit no-carry exponent identity and denominator valuation.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is the exact rational image/digit-language characterization, not the previously known cyclic-pair counting formula or fixed-order group rigidity. Chatterjee–Das 2026 derive the general cyclic-pair count and classify selected rational levels, but do not give the prime-power digit-word image criterion. Amiri 2026, extending Tărnăuceanu, proves fixed-order rigidity for the affinely equivalent sum of element orders of a p-group; that implication is expressly excluded from the claimed novelty. The one-zero separator pattern, complete iff-test for all reduced rational numbers and order-free explicit inverse are not asserted in the inspected primary sources. Distinct tests of aliases, weighted order sums, group-type rigidity and rational spectrum found no exact earlier characterization; independent historical priority is not certified.
residual_risks: Earlier work on numerical images of sums of element orders may contain an equivalent digit-pattern criterion not located here.
The relevant first-order cyclic-probability source and earlier sum-of-orders rigidity make uniqueness at a fixed order prior work, which must not be counted as new.
Some PDF page screenshots were unavailable; extracted text was inspected for the short 1993 original.

value.rationale: The complete set of cyclic-pair probability values is an explicit 2026 problem. Finite abelian p-groups form a canonical primary building block, and the theorem gives a complete arithmetical membership characterization of their noncyclic value set, not just a formula evaluated on selected groups. One reduced rational value supplies p, order, and every invariant factor by base-p digit inspection, with the exact value count P(n)-1 per reduced denominator. This is an exact natural spectrum classification with a constructive inverse and an independently checkable certificate; fixed-order injectivity alone would not suffice for value.
